objective: Write a learner-defined Python test function, with learner-written imports, that uses reusable valid, boundary and malformed fixtures to exercise the supplied packaged prediction function. Assert row count, feature/target correspondence and output shape before numerical comparisons with explicit tolerances, and test the declared exception path. Safely write and reload the supplied Cloud Build configuration, connect the test entry point to its assigned stage, and verify accepted and deliberately regressed runs through the configured repository commit trigger and branch filter.
success: The accepted fixtures pass all structural and numerical checks, and contract-prohibited inputs produce the declared exception. The reloaded configuration has the required execution image, command, step IDs and waitFor dependencies without failure allowances. A deliberate behavior regression produces an unsuccessful test-stage exit in an actual triggered run, and dependent later stages do not execute.

live_code.required_skill: Author reusable fixture-based assertions against a fitted prediction package and connect their executable entry point to an existing fatal test stage.
allowed_syntax: imports for the supplied prediction package
np.testing.assert_allclose with explicit rtol and atol
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide the supplied packaged prediction callable, its declared contract, fixture inputs and expected outputs using only the supplied example's existing names, the declared NumPy and PyYAML dependencies, and an existing authorized Cloud Build configuration and repository trigger. Leave the test function, imports, assertions and assigned-stage wiring for the learner to implement.
live_code.observable_success: Execution demonstrates structure checks before numerical comparisons, explicit tolerances, and assertions for valid, boundary and failure cases. Configuration inspection after safe reloading confirms the required resolved fields. Actual triggered stage results show an accepted run succeeding and an injected regression failing the test stage with dependent stages unexecuted.
